inScope: Implement and verify: Owner Settlement & Finance Dashboard.
Version contract, persistence, authorization, failure, audit, and operator behavior needed by this outcome.
Provide repository-specific automated tests and Postman/Newman evidence for callable APIs.

Direct cross-service database reads or duplicated ownership.
Unreviewed workflow transitions, historical rewrites, or destructive migration shortcuts.
businessRules: MANAGEMENT basis is verified collected lodging after discounts/refunds; exclude unearned deposit, staff markup, damage/cleaning, and employee commission.
OTA commission is included only when the effective contract says so.
LEASED uses fixed monthly amount with actual-day proration; OWNED produces no host payable.
Closed periods are immutable; reopen requires maker-checker reason and compensating history.
interfaces: Version GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/OpenAPI contracts before consumer implementation; document owner, caller, schema version, timeout, and compatibility.
Callable HTTP/GraphQL workflows include success, authorization-negative, validation, conflict, replay, and dependency-failure Postman examples.
Events use transactional outbox/inbox, stable aggregate identity, event ID, occurred-at time, producer schema version, and replay-safe consumers.
dataOwnership: Finance owns settlement periods, lines, adjustments, payable state, and exports; Property supplies effective immutable contract-term snapshots.
stateMachine: Model legal states and transitions for Owner Settlement & Finance Dashboard; reject illegal transitions with stable error codes.
Persist actor, reason, source, policy/contract version, expected revision, and timestamps for every material transition.
Terminal or superseded records are retained; corrections use a new revision or compensating record.

dataPartitions: SYSTEM for internal repair only; otherwise enforce the subject account type and the resource customer, host-party, site, branch, or assigned-employee partition.
fieldGroups: SUMMARY by default; FINANCIAL, PII, DOCUMENT, TRUST_DETAIL, and INTERNAL_AUDIT require explicit grants and response-field filtering.

failureSemantics: Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, stale-revision, dependency-unavailable, and rate-limit codes without leaking PII.
Fail closed when authorization, authoritative projection, policy version, or required dependency is unavailable.
Retry only transient operations with bounded exponential backoff; route exhausted asynchronous work to a visible repair queue.
idempotencyConcurrency: Every externally retried mutation requires a scoped idempotency key, canonical request fingerprint, durable result, and mismatch rejection.
Use expected revision or equivalent compare-and-swap; concurrent winners are deterministic and losers receive conflict with current revision.
Consumers deduplicate by event ID and business key and support replay without duplicating money, inventory, notification, or audit effects.

acceptanceCriteria.given: an authorized actor with a valid partition and a complete request for Owner Settlement & Finance Dashboard
acceptanceCriteria.when: the command or query is executed
acceptanceCriteria.then: the documented outcome, state revision, audit record, and contract response are produced deterministically

acceptanceCriteria.given: a caller missing the action, partition, or requested field-group grant
acceptanceCriteria.then: access is denied without leaking existence or restricted fields and the denial is auditable

acceptanceCriteria.given: the same mutation is replayed or two requests use the same expected revision
acceptanceCriteria.then: at most one business effect is committed and all responses are stable, explainable, and reconciled

tests: Unit tests cover rule boundaries, legal/illegal transitions, rounding/timezone where relevant, and stable error mapping.
Integration tests cover persistence constraints, authorization action+partition+field groups, outbox/inbox replay, and dependency failure.
Postman/Newman flow covers happy path, negative authorization, validation, conflict, idempotent replay, and a cleanup-safe deterministic fixture.
observability: Propagate trace and correlation IDs across GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/webhook boundaries without logging secrets or protected fields.
Emit transition, latency, error-code, replay/deduplication, dependency, and repair-queue metrics with bounded-cardinality labels.
Provide dashboard/alert thresholds and a runbook for stuck states, reconciliation mismatch, and rollback.

Contracts, migrations, compatibility path, implementation, Admin Web/Mobile parity where applicable, and Postman/Newman evidence are merged.

No production secret or unapproved monetary/policy default is committed; ServiceOwner acceptance evidence is attached before Done.

inScope: Implement and verify: Remediate settlement basis and contract-term calculations.
Version contract, persistence, authorization, failure, audit, and operator behavior needed by this outcome.
Provide repository-specific automated tests and Postman/Newman evidence for callable APIs.
outOfScope: Unlisted provider credentials and production policy values.
Direct cross-service database reads or duplicated ownership.
Unreviewed workflow transitions, historical rewrites, or destructive migration shortcuts.
businessRules: MANAGEMENT basis is verified collected lodging after discounts/refunds; exclude unearned deposit, staff markup, damage/cleaning, and employee commission.
OTA commission is included only when the effective contract says so.
LEASED uses fixed monthly amount with actual-day proration; OWNED produces no host payable.
Closed periods are immutable; reopen requires maker-checker reason and compensating history.
Create corrective settlement entries for already closed periods; never rewrite historical financial lines.
Link remediation evidence to the completed generic settlement implementation.
interfaces: Version GraphQL/gRPC/Kafka/OpenAPI contracts before consumer implementation; document owner, caller, schema version, timeout, and compatibility.
Callable HTTP/GraphQL workflows include success, authorization-negative, validation, conflict, replay, and dependency-failure Postman examples.
Events use transactional outbox/inbox, stable aggregate identity, event ID, occurred-at time, producer schema version, and replay-safe consumers.
dataOwnership: Finance owns settlement periods, lines, adjustments, payable state, and exports; Property supplies effective immutable contract-term snapshots.
stateMachine: Model legal states and transitions for Remediate settlement basis and contract-term calculations; reject illegal transitions with stable error codes.
Persist actor, reason, source, policy/contract version, expected revision, and timestamps for every material transition.
Terminal or superseded records are retained; corrections use a new revision or compensating record.

dataPartitions: SYSTEM for internal repair only; otherwise enforce the subject account type and the resource customer, host-party, site, branch, or assigned-employee partition.
fieldGroups: SUMMARY by default; FINANCIAL, PII, DOCUMENT, TRUST_DETAIL, and INTERNAL_AUDIT require explicit grants and response-field filtering.

failureSemantics: Return stable validation, forbidden, not-found, conflict, stale-revision, dependency-unavailable, and rate-limit codes without leaking PII.
Fail closed when authorization, authoritative projection, policy version, or required dependency is unavailable.
Retry only transient operations with bounded exponential backoff; route exhausted asynchronous work to a visible repair queue.
idempotencyConcurrency: Every externally retried mutation requires a scoped idempotency key, canonical request fingerprint, durable result, and mismatch rejection.
Use expected revision or equivalent compare-and-swap; concurrent winners are deterministic and losers receive conflict with current revision.
Consumers deduplicate by event ID and business key and support replay without duplicating money, inventory, notification, or audit effects.
